symptom: PC-A cannot reach Server-A in VLAN 30; gateway ping works.
topology_note: PC-A -> SW1 -> R1 -> Server-A; PC-A is assigned to VLAN 30.
show_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 30 not present on SW1.
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is missing from the switch.

symptom: PC-A in VLAN 20 cannot reach another host in VLAN 20.
topology_note: PC-A and PC-B are connected to SW1 and should be in VLAN 20.
show_outputs: show vlan brief: PC-A port is assigned to VLAN 10; PC-B port is VLAN 20.
expected_fault: PC-A access port is assigned to the wrong VLAN.

symptom: VLAN 30 hosts work locally but cannot cross SW1 to SW2.
topology_note: SW1 and SW2 are connected by a trunk.
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: VLANs allowed on trunk: 10,20; VLAN 30 absent.
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is not allowed on the trunk.

symptom: PCs in VLAN 40 cannot communicate with the switch gateway.
topology_note: PCs connect through SW1 to a router-on-a-stick gateway.
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: trunk is down; interface status shows Gi0/1 down.
expected_fault: The trunk interface is down.

symptom: A newly connected PC has no access to its assigned VLAN.
topology_note: PC-A is connected to SW1 Gi0/5 and should use VLAN 50.
show_outputs: show vlan brief: Gi0/5 is not assigned to VLAN 50.
expected_fault: The access port is not assigned to the required VLAN.

symptom: PC-A can communicate locally but cannot reach any remote network.
expected_fault: The default gateway is outside the host subnet.

symptom: PC-A has an IP address but cannot reach its gateway.
topology_note: PC-A is connected to the correct switch VLAN.
show_outputs: show ip interface brief on gateway: Gi0/0 192.168.10.1 is administratively down.
expected_fault: The gateway interface is administratively shut down.

symptom: PC-A can reach its gateway but not the server subnet.
topology_note: PC-A gateway is R1; server is on 10.10.20.0/24.
show_outputs: show ip route: no route to 10.10.20.0/24 and no default route.
expected_fault: R1 is missing a route to the server network.

symptom: PC-A has an IP but cannot reach devices outside its subnet.
expected_fault: The configured gateway is on a different subnet.

symptom: PC-A cannot access the network after a gateway address change.
topology_note: The LAN uses 192.168.5.0/24 and gateway should be 192.168.5.1.
show_outputs: ipconfig: IP 192.168.5.20 mask 255.255.255.0 gateway 192.168.5.254; gateway interface is 192.168.5.1.
expected_fault: PC-A has the wrong default gateway.

symptom: PC-A receives a 169.254.x.x address.
topology_note: PC-A should receive an address from the central DHCP server.
show_outputs: ipconfig: 169.254.10.25; show ip dhcp pool: no available leases; DHCP server reachable from router.
expected_fault: The DHCP pool has no available addresses.

symptom: PC-A receives no DHCP address across a routed network.
topology_note: DHCP server is on another subnet.
show_outputs: show run: DHCP relay/ip helper-address is missing on the client-facing interface.
expected_fault: DHCP relay configuration is missing.

symptom: PC-A receives an incorrect subnet from DHCP.
topology_note: DHCP scope should provide 192.168.30.0/24.
show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: network 192.168.40.0/24 configured instead of 192.168.30.0/24.
expected_fault: The DHCP pool is configured for the wrong network.

symptom: Clients get IP addresses but cannot use the intended gateway.
topology_note: DHCP should advertise 192.168.60.1 as the default gateway.
show_outputs: show run: default-router 192.168.70.1 in the VLAN 60 DHCP pool.
expected_fault: DHCP is advertising the wrong default gateway.

symptom: PC can ping the DNS server but website names do not resolve.
topology_note: PC has working IP connectivity to the DNS server.
show_outputs: ipconfig /all: DNS server 192.168.99.10; nslookup example.local: timeout.
expected_fault: The configured DNS service is not responding.

symptom: PC can access a server by IP but not by hostname.
topology_note: Network routing is working.
show_outputs: nslookup server.local: Server unknown; ping 10.10.10.20 succeeds.
expected_fault: DNS name resolution is failing.

symptom: Only some internal names fail to resolve.
topology_note: DNS server is reachable from clients.
show_outputs: nslookup app.internal: NXDOMAIN; nslookup dns.internal: successful.
expected_fault: The required DNS record is missing.

symptom: Router cannot reach a remote LAN.
topology_note: R1 connects to R2; remote LAN is 172.16.20.0/24.
show_outputs: show ip route: no 172.16.20.0/24 route.
expected_fault: A route to the remote LAN is missing.

symptom: Static route exists but traffic still fails.
topology_note: R1 should route to 10.20.0.0/24 through R2 at 10.0.0.2.
show_outputs: show ip route 10.20.0.0: route points to 10.0.0.3, which is not R2.
expected_fault: The static route has an incorrect next hop.

symptom: Remote network is unreachable after a router restart.
topology_note: Dynamic routing is expected between R1 and R2.
show_outputs: show ip ospf neighbor: no neighbors; show interfaces: R1-R2 link is down.
expected_fault: The routing adjacency is down because the inter-router interface is down.

symptom: Router has an OSPF neighbor but does not learn the expected LAN.
show_outputs: show ip ospf neighbor: FULL; show ip route: 192.168.50.0/24 absent.
expected_fault: The expected network is not being advertised into OSPF.

symptom: PC can reach its gateway but traffic to another VLAN is blocked.
topology_note: Inter-VLAN routing is configured on R1.
show_outputs: show access-lists: ACL denies 192.168.10.0/24 to 192.168.20.0/24.
expected_fault: An ACL is explicitly denying the inter-VLAN traffic.

symptom: Users cannot access the application server but other traffic works.
topology_note: Server is 10.10.10.50; ACL is applied inbound on the LAN interface.
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.10.10.50 eq 443.
expected_fault: The ACL blocks HTTPS traffic to the application server.

symptom: Guest users can access an internal server.
topology_note: Guest VLAN should only access the internet.
show_outputs: show access-lists: guest-to-internal ACL permits 192.168.50.0/24 to 10.0.0.0/8.
expected_fault: The guest isolation ACL is incorrectly permitting internal traffic.

symptom: A newly added ACL causes all outbound traffic to fail.
topology_note: The ACL should allow normal outbound web traffic.
show_outputs: show access-lists: implicit deny is reached because no permit statement matches the traffic.
expected_fault: The ACL lacks a required permit rule.

symptom: Internal users can reach the router but cannot access the internet.
topology_note: Private LAN addresses must be translated to the public interface.
show_outputs: show ip nat translations: empty; show run: no ip nat inside source rule.
expected_fault: NAT is not configured for the internal subnet.

symptom: Some internal hosts have internet access while others do not.
topology_note: NAT uses an access list to identify inside addresses.
show_outputs: show access-lists NAT-LAN: 192.168.10.0/24 permitted, 192.168.20.0/24 absent.
expected_fault: The NAT ACL does not include the second internal subnet.

symptom: Internet access fails after changing the WAN interface.
topology_note: R1 uses Gi0/1 as the outside interface.
show_outputs: show run: ip nat outside is configured on Gi0/0, while WAN is Gi0/1.
expected_fault: NAT outside is configured on the wrong interface.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi clients receive addresses but cannot access the internet.
topology_note: Wireless clients are mapped to the guest VLAN.
show_outputs: show vlan brief: AP uplink does not carry guest VLAN; show interfaces trunk: guest VLAN absent.
expected_fault: The AP uplink trunk is not carrying the guest VLAN.

symptom: Wireless clients connect to the SSID but cannot obtain an IP address.
topology_note: The wireless SSID should use the guest DHCP scope.
show_outputs: AP configuration shows SSID mapped to VLAN 30; DHCP scope is configured for VLAN 40.
expected_fault: The wireless SSID is mapped to the wrong VLAN.
